projectDetails.name: Luna
projectDetails.summary:
LUNA Game is an interactive 2D Mars exploration and survival game designed for children aged 7–12. Players become junior astronauts tasked with keeping a Mars research outpost operational for seven Martian days (Sols). Through exploration, problem-solving, and interactive missions, players learn how astronauts manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and energy while responding to real Mars environmental conditions.

The project integrates authentic NASA open datasets, including Mars environmental observations and solar activity data, to bring real space science into gameplay. Players can explore the Martian environment, interact with outpost facilities, monitor mission conditions, and make decisions that affect their crew's survival.

By transforming complex NASA scientific data into an engaging, educational gaming experience, LUNA makes planetary science more accessible to young learners. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, resource management, and an understanding of the real challenges of human exploration on Mars.
projectDetails.details:
LUNA is a browser-based Mars survival game that turns planetary science into an interactive experience. Players manage a Mars outpost’s resources and respond to environmental hazards, including a solar-radiation storm. The game combines its existing survival systems with NASA data: DONKI solar events inform the storm scenario, Perseverance MEDA observations provide a bounded temperature reference, Curiosity RAD measurements appear as scientific context, and NASA Mars Trek imagery enriches the map.

The project’s benefit is making complex space-science data approachable through play. Instead of presenting data only as charts or facts, LUNA lets players explore how environmental conditions can affect decisions at a Mars outpost. It is an educational experience and not a mission-planning or life-support simulator and aims to encourage curiosity about Mars exploration and the challenges of living beyond Earth.

We built the project with Next.js, and browser-based JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The game uses a Canvas-based interface and runs in a standard web browser; no specialized hardware is required. NASA sources include DONKI, the MEDA and RAD archives, and Mars Trek.

A creative part of the project is connecting real observations to familiar game mechanics while keeping the science traceable. We considered scientific accuracy, clear attribution, playability, performance, and resilience when data services are unavailable. For example, solar-event severity affects the storm mechanic, while RAD dose-rate measurements remain an informational reference rather than being converted into an unsupported gameplay value.

projectDetails.name: Earthify
projectDetails.summary: Throughout the course of the hackathon, Team Deuterium has worked in a synchronous manner to create a website that monitors fluctuations on the Earth's surface using existing NASA Earth models in order to conceive accurate and reliable readings, Earthify. Earthify utilizes a wide array of different variables that make it adept at fulfilling the challenge provided. The challenge asks for a project that monitors changes in the Earth's surface and classifies them as significant or minor. This is precisely what Team Deuterium has achieved in its Earth data tracking website. Earthify can be a vital tool for aspiring meteorologists, agriculturists, climate enthusiasts, and many more due to its ability to display complicated data in a digestible and understandable manner. Team Deuterium firmly believes that Earthify will have a profound impact on the field of climate science as a whole due to its versatility and ease of use.
projectDetails.details:
Earthify is a dynamic, interactive website that tracks the fluctuations of certain variables, such as air pressure, solar radiation, wind speed, and relative humidity, drawing its information straight from existing NASA Earth models. The process of using the website starts when the user inputs a specific location, filter, and date into the respective boxes. This allows the website to fetch information from NASA's official APIs, making it accurate and reliable. The user can then see an overlay of the filtered data over a map of the Earth.

The impact of this project is mainly directed towards agriculturists, meteorologists, and climate enthusiasts who need a quick visual demonstration of the changes in the Earth's atmosphere. Earthify’s main source code was written through the use of JavaScript React in VS Code. Artificial Intelligence was used as a development aid in order to act as a catalyst for our existing ideas, knowledge, and skills to speed up the process, alongside diminishing the margin of repetition. All implementation and a vast majority of the development were done purely by the programmer of Team Deuterium.

Our project is highly innovative, as it allows the user to filter out the variable that they want and displays a very appealing cover page. We considered ease of use, understandability, and pragmatic implementation when building the framework of our project. In terms of factors in the Earth's atmosphere, we used air pressure, solar radiation, wind speed, and relative humidity in order to provide users with a wide range of variables.

FloodWise Cambodia
projectDetails.summary:
FloodWise Cambodia is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers in flood-prone areas around Tonlé Sap Lake make more informed farming decisions. Floods can destroy crops when farmers are unaware of changing water conditions or when flooding occurs during critical growing stages. 
Using NASA Earth observation data, including rainfall, historical flood observations, soil moisture, and temperature, the platform transforms complex environmental information into accessible insights. Farmers can explore rainfall patterns, stay aware of observed flood conditions, and use the Crop Planning feature to compare crop growing suitability, potential risks, estimated growing costs, and possible economic losses. This helps them make better-informed decisions about crop selection and planting times.
FloodWise Cambodia aims to help farmers prepare for seasonal floods, reduce uncertainty, and minimize the risk of losing their harvest. Ultimately, we aim to protect farmers' livelihoods, prevent crop losses, and build a more resilient agricultural community in Cambodia.
projectDetails.details:
FloodWise Cambodia is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers in flood-prone areas around Tonlé Sap Lake make more informed farming decisions. Flooding can damage crops, disrupt growing seasons, and threaten farmers' livelihoods, especially when they lack accessible information about changing environmental conditions.

Our platform transforms complex NASA Earth observation data into understandable and useful agricultural insights. Farmers can explore rainfall patterns, examine historical satellite-observed flood conditions, and access relevant crop information to support their planting decisions. By selecting their province and location, farmers can explore environmental information relevant to their agricultural area, compare potential planting and harvesting timelines, and identify crop options that may be more suitable for local conditions. We also integrate a Telegram chatbot to make important information more accessible through a familiar communication platform.

The project focuses on five provinces surrounding Tonlé Sap Lake: Siem Reap, Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Thom, and Kampong Chhnang.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FloodWise Cambodia aims to reduce agricultural risks by helping farmers make better-informed decisions about what to plant and when to plant it. By making environmental information easier to understand, the platform can help farmers prepare for seasonal flooding, reduce potential crop losses, and protect their livelihoods. In the long term, we hope to contribute to more resilient agricultural communities and encourage the use of satellite-based data in local agricultural planning.

Tools and Technologies

The tools we use are Artificial Intelligence technologies for information and project ideas (ChatGPT Plus, Astra 6, Claude Code, Codex), and the main tool we use is Python for information hooking, filtering, and cleaning.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes FloodWise Cambodia creative is the way it connects NASA satellite observations with practical agricultural decision-making. Instead of simply displaying scientific datasets, we aim to translate environmental information into insights that farmers can understand and use. Combining an interactive website with a Telegram chatbot also provides different ways for users to access information, making the project more accessible and practical.

Factors Considered

During development, we considered the local agricultural context, seasonal flooding patterns, the geographical differences between provinces, the accessibility of technology for farmers, and the importance of presenting information in a simple and understandable way. We also considered data reliability and limitations, particularly the distinction between historical satellite-observed flooding and actual future flood forecasts. FloodWise Cambodia does not claim to predict exact flood dates using historical satellite observations. Instead, it provides environmental information to support better-informed planning decisions.
